To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

chronic hyperendothelin-1 (HET-1) induces a decrease in the sensitivity of small arteries to contractile agonist, and that in cerebral arteries this is due to an increased endothelial alpha2-receptor-mediated stimulation of endothelial ET-1 secretion.

chronic elevated plasma ET-1 induces vascular hyporesponsiveness to contractile agonist in small arteries, and that this hyporesponsiveness may be due, at least in part, to an enhanced endothelial alpha2-receptor-mediated ET-1 release.

chronic hyperendothelinemic rats have a decreased sensitivity to contractile agents in both cerebral and mesenteric small arteries and that endothelial alpha2-receptor stimulation is more effective in inducing contraction in hyperendothelinic rats.

the effects of hyperendothelialinemia on vascular tone and suggests a potential role for ET-1 in the pathophysiology of hypertension.
the consequences of increased plasma ET-1 levels on vascular reactivity.
the effects of ET-1 on the vascular system.

the chronic elevation of plasma ET-1 levels leads to an increased sensitivity of vascular smooth muscle cells to contractile agonist and to a decreased responsiveness to alpha2-adrenoceptors.

the chronic elevation of ET-1 levels in plasma induces a decrease in smooth muscle cell sensitivity in small arteries, which may be a compensatory mechanism to maintain blood pressure in the presence of hyperendothelins.
the chronic hyperendotelinemia observed in this study induces an endothelium-mediated decrease in the sensitivity to contractile agents of small resistance arteries.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
chronic elevated plasmic ET-1 induces vascular dysfunction, which could contribute to the pathogenesis of cardiovascular disorders.

the chronic elevation of plasma ET-1 in vivo induces an endothelium-dependent potentiation of alpha2-adrenoceptors in the MCA, which may represent a compensating mechanism for the decrease in smooth muscle sensitivity.

the chronic elevation of ET-1 in plasma is associated with a decreased smooth muscle cell responsiveness to contractile agonist and a compensatory increase in endothelial ET-1 release in cerebral arteries.
The main takeaway from our work is that
chronic ET-1 hyperproduction in rats is associated with a decreased smooth muscle responsiveness to contractile stimuli.
chronic elevation of plasma ET-1 levels decreases smooth muscle responsiveness to contractile agonist.
